sentences.en: PROFESSOR: Good morning everyone
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: In today's seminar, Grant Freeman, a biologist who specialises in identifying insects, and who works for the Australian +
sentences.zh: 今天研讨会上，我们邀请到了格兰特·弗里曼先生，一位专长于昆虫鉴定的生物学家，就职于澳大利亚 录音稿+。

sentences.en: SLAB Quarantine Service, has come to talk to Us work
sentences.zh: SLAB检疫服务处，他将为我们介绍相关工作。

sentences.en: Right, well, over to you, Grant
sentences.zh: 好的，那么接下来交由你来主讲，格兰特。

sentences.en: I'm sure that you know that the quarantine service regulates all food brought into Australia
sentences.zh: 我相信大家都知道，澳大利亚检疫部门负责监管所有进入澳大利亚的食品。

sentences.en: Well, obviously they want to protect Australia from diseases that might come in with imported goods, but they also want to prevent insect pests from being introduced into the country, and that's where I have a part to play
sentences.zh: 显然，他们旨在保护澳大利亚免受随进口货物传入的疾病威胁；此外，他们还希望防止害虫昆虫被带入本国，而这正是我所承担的工作内容。

sentences.en: Anyway, my current a research involves trying to find a particular type of bee, the Asian Honey Bee, and finding out whether there are any of them around in various states of Australia
sentences.zh: 目前，我的研究工作主要致力于寻找一种特定类型的蜜蜂——亚洲蜜蜂，并调查澳大利亚各州是否已出现该类蜜蜂。

sentences.en: We discovered a few of them in Queensland once and eradicated them
sentences.zh: 我们曾于昆士兰州发现过少量亚洲蜜蜂，并已将其彻底清除。

sentences.en: Now, we're pretty keen to make sure that there aren't any more getting in, particularly to New South Wales and other states
sentences.zh: 如今，我们非常关注防止此类蜜蜂再度入境，尤其是进入新南威尔士州及其他各州。

sentences.en: STUDENT 1: What's wrong with Asian Honey Bees?
sentences.zh: STUDENT 1: 亚洲蜜蜂有什么问题？

sentences.en: Are they so different from Australian bees?
sentences.zh: 它们与澳大利亚本土蜜蜂差别真有那么大吗？

sentences.en: GRANT: Well, in fact, they look almost the same, but they are infested with mites microscopic creatures which live on them, and which can seriously damage our own home-grown bees, or could even wipe them out
sentences.zh: GRANT: 实际上，它们外形几乎完全相同，但其体表寄生着螨虫——一类微小生物，会严重危害我们本土养殖的蜜蜂，甚至可能导致其灭绝。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: Well, what would happen if Australian bees died out?
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 那么，倘若澳大利亚本土蜜蜂全部灭绝，将会发生什么情况？

sentences.en: GRANT: Well, the honey from Australian bees is of excellent quality, much better than the stuff the Asian bees produce
sentences.zh: GRANT: 首先，澳大利亚本土蜜蜂所产蜂蜜品质极佳，远优于亚洲蜜蜂所产蜂蜜。

sentences.en: In fact, Australia exports native Queen bees to a large number of countries because of this
sentences.zh: 事实上，正因如此，澳大利亚向众多国家出口本土蜂王。

sentences.en: When the European Honey Bee was first discovered out in the bush, we found they made really unpleasant honey and they were also too big to pollinate many of our native flowers here in Australia
sentences.zh: 当欧洲蜜蜂最初在澳洲丛林中被发现时，我们发现它们所酿蜂蜜口感极差，且体型过大，无法为澳大利亚许多本土花卉完成授粉。

sentences.en: STUDENT 2: That must have had a devastating effect on the natural flora
sentences.zh: STUDENT 2: 这必然对当地自然植被造成了毁灭性影响。

sentences.en: Did you lose any species?
sentences.zh: 你们因此丧失了某些植物物种吗？

sentences.en: GRANT: No, we managed to get them under control before that happened but if Asian bees got in there could be other consequences
sentences.zh: GRANT: 幸运的是，在事态恶化之前，我们成功控制住了欧洲蜜蜂；但若亚洲蜜蜂一旦入侵，可能引发其他严重后果。

sentences.en: We could lose a lot of money because you might not be aware, but it's estimated that native bees' pollination of flower and vegetable crops is worth 1.2 billion dollars a year
sentences.zh: 我们可能会损失大量资金，因为您可能并不知晓，但据估计，本土蜜蜂对花卉和蔬菜作物的授粉价值每年高达12亿美元。

sentences.en: So in a way they're the farmers' friend
sentences.zh: 因此，从某种意义上说，它们是农民的朋友。

sentences.en: Oh, and another thing is, if you're stung by an Asian Honey Bee, it can produce an allergic reaction in some people; so they're much more dangerous than native bees
sentences.zh: 哦，还有一点：如果您被亚洲蜜蜂蜇伤，某些人可能会产生过敏反应；因此，它们比本土蜜蜂危险得多。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: How will you know if Asian bees have entered Australia?
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 如果亚洲蜜蜂进入澳大利亚，你们将如何识别？

sentences.en: GRANT: We're looking at the diet of the bird called the Rainbow Bee Eater
sentences.zh: GRANT: 我们正在研究一种名为彩虹蜂虎鸟的鸟类的食谱。

sentences.en: The Bee Eater doesn't care what it eats, as long as they're insects
sentences.zh: 蜂虎鸟并不挑剔所吃的食物，只要它们是昆虫即可。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing about this bird is that we are able to analyse exactly what it eats and that's really helpful if we're looking for introduced insects
sentences.zh: 但这种鸟的有趣之处在于，我们能够精确分析它所吃的食物，而这一点在我们搜寻外来昆虫时非常有帮助。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: How come?
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 这是为什么？

sentences.en: GRANT: Because insects have their skeletons outside their bodies, SO the Bee Eaters digest the meat from the inside
sentences.zh: GRANT: 因为昆虫的骨骼长在身体外部，所以蜂虎鸟会从内部消化昆虫的肉质部分。

sentences.en: Then they bring up all the indigestible bits of skeleton and, of course, the wings in a pellet a small ball of waste material which they cough up
sentences.zh: 随后，它们会将无法消化的外骨骼残渣以及翅膀以食丸形式反刍出来——即一小团废物，它们会将其咳出。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: a That sounds a bit unpleasant
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 听起来有点令人不适。

sentences.en: So, how do you go about it?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们具体是如何操作的呢？

sentences.en: GRANT: In the field we track down the Bee Eaters and find their favourite feeding spots, you know, the places where the birds usually feed
sentences.zh: GRANT: 在野外，我们会追踪蜂虎鸟并找到它们最偏爱的觅食地点，也就是这些鸟类通常觅食的地方。

sentences.en: It's here that we can find the pellets
sentences.zh: 正是在这些地方，我们可以找到那些食丸。

sentences.en: We collect them up and take them back to the laboratory to examine the contents
sentences.zh: 我们收集这些食丸并带回实验室，以检查其中的内容物。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: How do you do that?
sentences.zh: PROFESSOR: 你们如何进行检查？

sentences.en: Then we pull them apart under the microscope
sentences.zh: 接着，我们在显微镜下将它们逐一分解。

sentences.en: Everything's all scrunched up but we're looking for wings so we just pull them all out and straighten them
sentences.zh: 所有东西都挤作一团，但我们主要寻找的是翅膀，因此只需将它们全部取出并展平即可。

sentences.en: Then we identify them to see if we can find any Asian bee wings
sentences.zh: 然后我们对它们进行鉴定，看看是否能找到任何亚洲蜜蜂的翅膀。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: And how many have you found?
sentences.zh: 教授：你们找到了多少只？

sentences.en: GRANT: So far our research shows that Asian bees have not entered Australia in any number - it's a good result and much more reliable than trying to find live ones as evidence of introduced insects
sentences.zh: 格兰特：到目前为止，我们的研究表明，亚洲蜜蜂尚未以任何数量进入澳大利亚——这是一个很好的结果，而且比试图找到活体蜜蜂作为外来昆虫入侵的证据要可靠得多。

sentences.en: PROFESSOR: Well, that's fascinating!
sentences.zh: 教授：嗯，这真令人着迷！

sentences.en: Thank you, Grant, for those insights
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的这些见解，格兰特。

sentences.en: I hope that you might inspire some of our students here to conduct some similar experiments
sentences.zh: 我希望你今天分享的内容或许能激励在座的一些同学开展类似的实验。
